nodes.title: Round 8 Play P1: the play server chooses the game from what she holds. One pure picker (server/play/choose.js chooseEntry) over every coverage entry admitting the skill (across families and modes), not the first entry: score = 2·info + fit + novelty, info = Σ over the mix-ups the entry's garam level discriminates (its own misMap) of max(0, P(mis) − 0.15) (+1 for the active belief), fit = −|pFirstTry − 0.75| when her pL is known, novelty = −0.3 each for a family/mode, entry or level signature she just played; the best entry is served when it beats the first by 0.1, otherwise the first. An active belief (the lesson's focus, else a mapped P(mis) > 0.5) becomes the session focus, so the FIRST level (garam) tests it, not a door. Nothing known (no mapped mis above prior, no focus, no pL) = the first entry, exactly as before, with no level generated for the others. Every departure carries a because {choice, fact, source} (fact = the kit's belief text), stored on the signed session body and returned by /api/play/start, /level and the forge live seam; the chosen entry key stays in the session so every route regenerates the same level. The lesson's forge seam no longer pins compose's goal when a skill is known (compose's rung is the first entry, so the default is unchanged) and passes the last shown family as novelty. Why: 269 of 744 admitted skills have 2-4 games and the server always served the first, so an open mix-up only one of them can show was never tested first. Reverse if: cross-family pFirstTry (uncalibrated per family) makes the fit term move children to a family whose measured first-try rate is outside 0.6-0.9 on 20+ levels (then drop fit across families, keep info); or children's game evidence after a belief-chosen family confirms/clears the belief no faster than the first-entry family over 50 sessions (then serve the first entry and keep the belief as its focus only); or the literature lever (adaptive-sequencing-as-the-lever) is measured here as no gain and the cost matters.

md.decisions:
## `dc-r8-play-pick-the-game` (2026-11-10)

Round 8 Play P1. The play server chooses the game from what she holds: one pure picker, `server/play/choose.js` `chooseEntry`, over every coverage entry admitting the skill.

- **Score** = 2·info + fit + novelty. info = Σ over the mix-ups the entry's garam level discriminates (own misMap) of max(0, P(mis) − 0.15), +1 for the active belief. fit = −|pFirstTry − 0.75| when her pL is known. novelty = −0.3 each for a family/mode, entry or level signature she just played.
- The best entry is served when it beats the first entry by 0.1; otherwise the first.
- An active belief (the lesson's focus, else a mapped P(mis) > 0.5) becomes the session focus, so the first level tests it.
- Nothing known = the first entry, exactly as before; no level is generated for the others.
- Every departure carries `because: {choice, fact, source}` (fact from the kit's belief text), on the signed session and returned by `/api/play/start`, `/level` and the forge live seam.

**Why:** 269 of 744 admitted skills have 2-4 games and the server always served the first.

**Reverse if:**
- the fit term (pFirstTry is uncalibrated across families) moves children to a family whose measured first-try rate is outside 0.6-0.9 over 20+ levels: drop fit across families, keep info;
- a belief-chosen family confirms or clears the belief no faster than the first-entry family over 50 sessions: serve the first entry with the belief as its focus only.
